body: This issue persists in CLI11 v2.6.2.

Below is the minimum reproductional example.
As you can see, .calling `/cli11_help_bug subc1 subc2 --help` provides help on subc1, not subc2.

```shell
$> ./cli11_help_bug subc1 --help
First subcommand


./cli11_help_bug subc1 [OPTIONS] ID [SUBCOMMAND]


POSITIONALS:
  ID INT REQUIRED             Object ID

OPTIONS:
  -h,     --help              Print this help message and exit

SUBCOMMANDS:
  subc2                       Nested subcommand
$> ./cli11_help_bug subc1 subc2 --help
First subcommand


./cli11_help_bug subc1 [OPTIONS] ID [SUBCOMMAND]


POSITIONALS:
  ID INT REQUIRED             Object ID

OPTIONS:
  -h,     --help              Print this help message and exit

SUBCOMMANDS:
  subc2                       Nested subcommand
```

### Reproduction example

```c++
#include <CLI/CLI.hpp>

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    CLI::App app{"CLI11 help bug MRE"};

    auto* subc1 = app.add_subcommand("subc1", "First subcommand");

    int id{};
    subc1->add_option("ID", id, "Object ID")->required();

    auto* subc2 = subc1->add_subcommand("subc2", "Nested subcommand");

    bool flag{false};
    subc2->add_flag("--flag", flag, "Example flag");

    CLI11_PARSE(app, argc, argv);

    return 0;
}
```

Adding positional argument:
```
$ ./cli11_help_bug subc1 1 subc2 --help
Nested subcommand


./cli11_help_bug subc1 subc2 [OPTIONS]


OPTIONS:
  -h,     --help              Print this help message and exit
          --flag              Example flag
```
